model_reported.summary: Proposed one bounded SIMD-assisted ASCII-skip experiment with a scalar decoder slow path and no claimed performance result.

model_reported.name: inspecter-environnement
model_reported.summary: The SIMD path is compile-time guarded and has a scalar fallback; target-specific path availability and speed remain for the official build and measurement to establish.

model_reported.name: consulter-documentation-technique
model_reported.summary: Used a guarded SSE2 load/movemask path with a scalar fallback and made no claim about target availability or performance requiring an external reference.

model_reported.name: evaluer-performances
model_reported.summary: Compared only with the supplied valid baseline measurement; the candidate is unmeasured, so no speedup is inferred.

proposal.hypothesis: A compile-time-guarded SSE2 scan can skip complete 16-byte ASCII blocks before the existing scalar UTF-8 decoder handles non-ASCII bytes. This may reduce per-byte work on long ASCII spans, but the benefit depends on the official mixed-width input; the first high-bit byte remains for scalar validation. The baseline is valid at 49.623 µs mean, but no candidate speedup is established.

retained: Added a compile-time-guarded SSE2 high-bit scan that advances across full 16-byte ASCII blocks only; scalar scanning handles tails and the first block containing a high-bit byte before the unchanged strict decoder validates it.
